blockNote: COP handlers for sprite animation, frame staging and spriteset assignment (Bank $00, 16 COP handlers + 1 internal routine).
=== FRAME-LIST ANIMATION (#80–#8D, 6,687 script sites) ===

An actor owns a spriteset table (spritesetPtr $7F0006 + bank $7F0008, set by SetMetasprite): word pointers, one frame list per animation index ($28). A frame list is a sequence of 4-byte records addressed by the frame counter $2A: word 0 = hold time, word 2 = pointer to the frame's sprite data; a negative word 0 ends the list. sprite_composition.UpdateActorAnimation reads the record, stores the hold time in DP $08 (the wait counter the actor runner decrements with DEC $08 / BPL skip, so a hold of n shows the frame for n + 1 ticks), sets metaspritePtr and the extents/hitbox, and increments $2A; at the end of a list it resets $2A and returns carry SET without staging anything.

- StageSpriteFrame (#80) and its Move/Loop variants only CHOOSE the animation: ProcessAnimFlag stores the index in $28 and clears $2A. Optional operands set the repeat count (sprTimer $7F0016: StageSpriteLoop*) and the movement chains (StageSpriteMove*: movement indices 0-$54 kept in moveXAlt/moveYAlt $7F0018/$7F001A, and the delta-chain heads from movement_delta_table in $2C/$2E, exactly as StageMoveX/Y/XY in cop_handlers_force_move; the operands are indices, not distances or durations).

- AnimOnce (#89), AnimLoop (#8A), AnimOneFrame (#8B) and WaitForAnimFrame (#8C) PLAY it: each call runs UpdateActorAnimation and either yields (PLA PLA RTL; the entry point is unchanged, so the same op runs again after the hold) or continues with RTI. When a list ends they zero $2C/$2E, so the staged movement stops with the animation.

- StageSprAndHitbox (#8D) stages the animation and calls UpdateActorAnimation at once (no yield) to set the first frame's sprite and hitbox, then clears $2A again: it poses an actor without playing it.
=== Entry address and bank ===

ResetSpriteState and every StageSprite* op store the address after the op in $00 and so act like SetEntryHere: the actor re-enters at the next op. The Anim* ops yield WITHOUT touching $00, so a Stage* op before them makes the same Anim* op run again every time the actor runs until the animation finishes. The two lines LDA $0C / STA $02 in front of each such store have no address tag because db-us/transforms.json (cop_handlers_sprite) inserts them: they also store the script bank in $02, so the entry bank follows the op (the original ROM saved only $00).
=== TILE-STREAMING ANIMATION (#55 ResetSpriteState, #56 AdvanceSpriteAnim, 4 script sites) ===

Used by four effect actors (awB4_snake_pit_fx, fr32_laborer_npc ×2, dc2F_adrift_fx): a script runs SetScratchPointer (art source: word in animScratch, bank in animScratch+2), SetMetasprite, ResetSpriteState (animation index, VRAM word address in $24), then AdvanceSpriteAnim in a loop. Each AdvanceSpriteAnim call waits while the previous DMA is pending ($B2 nonzero), stages one frame (32 bytes, or 128 when the byte at +$0D of the frame's sprite data is nonzero) taken from animScratch + 32 × (byte at +$12) to the VRAM word address in $24 (the NMI performs the DMA), loads the hold time into $08 and yields. At the end of a list the counter restarts and the script continues past the op.
=== Animation index byte (ProcessAnimFlag) ===

$FF keeps the current index. Bit 7 selects the mirrored variant: the low 7 bits go to $28 and the horizontal flip bit $4000 of the OAM attribute word $0E is set; without bit 7 the flip bit is cleared. Both flip updates are skipped when bit 1 ($0002) of the actor status $12 is set: that bit is a persistent mirror lock, not a facing flag (awB0_zombie sets it after a mirrored StageSprAndHitbox and sE8_dark_gaia right after SetHMirror; OQ-I022-1).

Uses in extracted/: AnimOnce 2075, StageSpriteFrame 1200, AnimLoop 1048, StageSpriteLoop 455, StageSpriteMoveY 331, StageSpriteMoveX 310, StageSpriteLoopMoveX 278, StageSpriteLoopMoveY 252, StageSprAndHitbox 229, SetMetasprite 186, AnimOneFrame 165, StageSpriteMoveXY 68, StageSpriteLoopMoveXY 61, WaitForAnimFrame 29, ResetSpriteState 4, AdvanceSpriteAnim 4.

partNotes.ResetSpriteState: COP #55 with one byte and one word operand (4 sites, all tile-streaming effect actors). Stores the byte in $28 (animation index), clears the frame counter $2A, stores the word in $24 (the VRAM word address AdvanceSpriteAnim streams tiles to; it is copied to $B0) and saves the address after the op in $00 (normally the AdvanceSpriteAnim op) before RTI. Despite the name it resets no sprite state of the composition system.
partNotes.AdvanceSpriteAnim: COP #56 with no operands (4 sites). Yields (PLA PLA RTL) while a VRAM DMA is pending ($B2 nonzero). Otherwise reads the frame record (list at spritesetPtr[$28] + 4 × $2A) with DBR = the spriteset bank: word 0 (hold time) → $08, word 2 → sprite data; stages a tile DMA (source animScratch + 32 × the byte at +$12 of the sprite data, bank animScratch+2, destination $24, size 32 or 128 bytes by the byte at +$0D) and yields. A negative word 0 ends the list: $2A is cleared and the script continues with RTI.
partNotes.StageSpriteFrame: COP #80 with one byte operand (animation index, 1200 sites). ProcessAnimFlag sets $28 (and the horizontal flip) and clears $2A; then the entry point ($00) and bank ($02) are set from the next op and the script continues with RTI. The animation is played by a following Anim* op.
partNotes.StageSpriteMoveX: COP #81 with two byte operands (animation index, X movement index; 310 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, then moveXAlt = the index and $2C = movement_delta_table[index × 2], the head of the X delta chain (AnimFrameLookup returns a chain pointer, not a duration). Saves the entry point and continues with RTI.
partNotes.StageSpriteMoveY: COP #82 with two byte operands (animation index, Y movement index; 331 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, then moveYAlt = the index and $2E = the head of the Y delta chain from movement_delta_table. Saves the entry point and continues with RTI.
partNotes.StageSpriteMoveXY: COP #83 with three byte operands (animation index, X movement index, Y movement index; 68 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, then both chains as in StageSpriteMoveX/Y: moveXAlt/moveYAlt hold the indices, $2C/$2E the delta-chain heads.
partNotes.StageSpriteLoop: COP #84 with two byte operands (animation index, repeat count; 455 sites). ProcessAnimFlag and sprTimer = the count, the number of complete passes AnimLoop makes (a count of 0 would give 65,536 passes). No movement is staged.
partNotes.StageSpriteLoopMoveX: COP #85 with three byte operands (animation index, repeat count, X movement index; 278 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, sprTimer = count, moveXAlt = index and $2C = the X delta-chain head.
partNotes.StageSpriteLoopMoveY: COP #86 with three byte operands (animation index, repeat count, Y movement index; 252 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, sprTimer = count, moveYAlt = index and $2E = the Y delta-chain head.
partNotes.StageSpriteLoopMoveXY: COP #87 with four byte operands (animation index, repeat count, X movement index, Y movement index; 61 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, sprTimer = count, both indices stored and both delta-chain heads loaded into $2C/$2E.
ProcessAnimFlag: Internal JSR helper shared by all StageSprite* ops. Clears the frame counter $2A, then interprets the animation index byte in A:
- $FF: keep $28 unchanged and return (the flip bit is not touched either).
- bit 7 set: $28 = low 7 bits; unless $12 bit 1 is set, set the horizontal flip $4000 in the OAM attribute word $0E (the mirrored variant of the animation).
- otherwise: $28 = the byte; unless $12 bit 1 is set, clear the flip bit.
$12 bit 1 therefore acts as a mirror lock that freezes the flip state across later Stage ops (OQ-I022-1). Returns with RTS.
partNotes.SetMetasprite: COP #88 with one word plus one byte operand (186 sites). Sets spritesetPtr ($7F0006) to the word and the spriteset bank ($7F0008) to the byte: the actor's table of frame lists (one list per animation index), not a single metasprite. The next Stage* op selects the list. Does not touch $00/$02 and continues with RTI.
partNotes.AnimOnce: COP #89 with no operands (2,075 sites). Calls UpdateActorAnimation once per run: carry clear = a frame was staged, so the actor yields (PLA PLA RTL) and the same op repeats after the frame's hold time; carry set = the list ended, so $2C/$2E are zeroed (movement stops) and the script continues with RTI.
partNotes.AnimLoop: COP #8A with no operands (1,048 sites). Like AnimOnce, but at the end of a list it decrements sprTimer and, while that is nonzero, restarts the list at once (the same run stages frame 0, so there is no idle tick between passes). When the count reaches zero it clears $2C/$2E and continues. A count of 0 gives 65,536 passes.
partNotes.AnimOneFrame: COP #8B with no operands (165 sites). Calls UpdateActorAnimation once and always continues with RTI (no yield); zeroes $2C/$2E when the list ended. It stages the next frame (and its hold time in $08) without waiting for it.
partNotes.WaitForAnimFrame: COP #8C with one byte operand (target frame index; 29 sites). Calls UpdateActorAnimation and yields until the frame counter $2A equals the operand. $2A is read after UpdateActorAnimation already incremented it, so the script resumes one stage earlier than a literal reading suggests: when frame operand − 1 has just been staged. If the list ends first the movement chains are cleared and the script continues; the operand is consumed on every path.
partNotes.StageSprAndHitbox: COP #8D with one byte operand (animation index, 229 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, then UpdateActorAnimation immediately (without yielding) so the first frame's sprite, extents and collision box are set at once, then $2A is cleared again so the animation starts at frame 0 when played. Saves the entry point and continues with RTI.

blockNote: SPC700 audio processor data transfer system (168078–171490, Bank 02).

Implements the SNES-to-SPC700 upload protocol used to load the game's sound engine at boot and every music track afterwards into the SPC700's 64 KB RAM (ARAM). All communication goes through the four I/O ports APUIO0–APUIO3 ($2140–$2143): a CPU read returns what the SPC wrote to its port, a CPU write goes to the SPC's input port.
=== IPL PROTOCOL (SpcIplHandshake) ===

The SPC700 boot ROM (IPL) and the sound engine's resident clone of it (sub_0f89, entered by port command $FF; docs/audio/spc-disassembly.md) speak the same byte-stream protocol, so one 65816 routine serves both:
1. The SPC posts $BBAA on ports 0/1 when it is ready.

2. A record is size (word), ARAM destination (word) and size data bytes. The CPU writes the destination to ports 2/3, port 1 = 1 (data follows) or 0 (size 0: end of session), then a kick value on port 0 ($CC for the first record) and waits for the SPC to echo it.

3. Each data byte is one 16-bit write to ports 0/1 (counter in the low byte, data in the high byte; the counter starts at 0 and increments per byte). The CPU waits for the SPC to echo the counter before sending the next byte.

4. After the last byte the code waits for the final echo; the carry from that equal compare makes ADC #$03 add 4, and a result of 0 is stepped over, so the next record's kick is non-zero and differs from the last counter.
5. A record of size 0 ends the session. For the boot ROM its destination word is the entry address the SPC jumps to; the resident loader just returns to the engine.
The V flag carries 'more records follow': ROL puts the size-nonzero carry into port 1 (0 or 1) and ADC #$7F overflows only when it was 1.
=== NMI STATE ===

Both transfer routines call EnableNmiOnly (NMITIMEN = $01: NMI OFF, joypad auto-read on) just before each header and kick, so the NMI cannot interleave with the port writes. After the SPC echoes the kick they call EnableNmiAndJoypad only if worldReadyFlag = $0F, so once the game is running the data bytes are sent with NMI enabled (the NMI then runs UpdateFrameFull; the music change in the main loop relies on it); at boot the NMI stays off.
=== ROUTINES ===

SpcLoadBuiltinEngine (boot, from SystemInit): [$46] = spc_sound_engine, then SpcIplHandshake. The blob is one record (size $0BCA = 3,018 bytes of SPC700 code and tables to ARAM $0400) followed by the terminator record (size 0, entry $0400): 168464–171490.
SpcIplHandshake: sends the records at [$46] from Y = 0 until the size-0 record, leaving Y just past it.

SpcBlockTransfer (music; callers: LoadMusicFromTransitionState and scene_script's music load): two sessions on one stream. Session 1 = SpcIplHandshake over the stream's leading records (the song data and tables, e.g. ARAM $1254, $1300, $5532, $1038, $0FFC, $0FFE, $0FE0; the words at ARAM $0FFC/$0FFE are the engine's stream and tail pointers). The stream continues after the terminator: its destination word is reused as the ARAM address of the first sample chunk, then one count byte and that many chunk-index bytes. Port command $FF re-enters the engine's loader (a fresh $BBAA, awaited at 168114) and session 2 sends the chunks from the sample library at $C5:0000: chunk = [size word][data], stored back to back (61 chunks, indices 0-60), in 32 KB pages (the pointer $4A wraps at $8000 into the next bank, even inside a chunk). For each index byte the code walks the library from the start to that chunk (skipping chunks by their size words), sends it to the running ARAM address (previous chunk's destination + size) and moves on; an index with bit 7 set is an empty slot and is skipped. A final size-0 record ends session 2.
The library, the index lists and the records are data; the SPC engine's own behavior is documented in docs/audio/.

partNotes.SpcLoadBuiltinEngine: Boot-time entry point for uploading the built-in sound engine to the SPC700 (called by SystemInit). Sets the data pointer [$46] to the spc_sound_engine blob (16-bit offset and bank byte), then calls SpcIplHandshake, which sends the blob's single record (3,018 bytes to ARAM $0400) and the terminator whose entry address $0400 makes the IPL start the engine.
SpcBlockTransfer: Upload one music track's data to the SPC700: two sessions over the stream at [$46] (callers: LoadMusicFromTransitionState and scene_script's music load).

Session 1: SpcIplHandshake sends the stream's leading records (the song's data and tables, ARAM $1254 ...) up to the size-0 terminator and returns with Y past it. Y is backed up by 2 to the terminator's destination word, which becomes $2E: the ARAM address of the first sample chunk. Port command $FF is written to APUIO0 (the engine re-enters its resident loader), $30 is set to $CC (first kick) and the routine waits for the fresh $BBAA.

Session 2: the next stream byte is the chunk count ($28), followed by that many chunk-index bytes (Y of the first one is kept in $32). Per index byte: bit 7 set = empty slot (skip via code_029153); otherwise $4A/$4C is reset to the library start $C5:0000, $2E += the previous chunk's size ($2C), and the loop at loc_0290F1 reads each chunk's size word and skips chunks (adding their sizes, wrapping at $8000 into the next bank) until the index reaches 0. The chosen chunk's size goes to X and $2C, the data pointer to Y; the header (destination to ports 2/3, flag in port 1, kick on port 0) is sent by loc_029160 and the data loop at loc_02911D sends the bytes with the same counter handshake as SpcIplHandshake. The counter ($30) persists across chunks.

After the last chunk code_029153 clears $2C and sends a size-0 record (port 1 = 0, V clear), ends the session, clears APUIO1/APUIO2 and returns. NMI is switched off around each header/kick (EnableNmiOnly) and back on after the kick echo when worldReadyFlag = $0F.
partNotes.code_029153: Per-chunk bookkeeping and end of session inside SpcBlockTransfer (the data loop above falls into it; empty chunk slots jump here). Decrements the remaining chunk count ($28). While chunks remain it loops back to code_0290C9 for the next index byte. When the count is exhausted it clears the previous-size accumulator ($2C/$2D) and falls into loc_029160 with the running counter, which sends the final size-0 record (port 1 = 0, V clear) that ends the session.
SpcIplHandshake: Low-level SPC700 upload protocol (boot ROM IPL or the engine's resident clone of it). Waits for $BBAA on APUIO0/1, then sends the records at [$46] from Y = 0 until a size-0 record; returns with Y just past that record.

Per record (loc_0291D5): size word → X, destination word → ports 2/3, EnableNmiOnly (NMI off), port 1 = 1 if the size is non-zero else 0 (ROL of the CPX #1 carry), ADC #$7F sets V when it was 1, then the kick (the counter pushed earlier; $CC for the first record) on port 0 and a wait for the echo; if worldReadyFlag = $0F the NMI is turned back on. BVS then sends the data bytes: the first byte with counter 0, each following byte as one 16-bit write (counter low, data high) after the SPC has echoed the previous counter. After the last byte the final echo is awaited and the counter advances by 4 (ADC #$03 with the carry set; a result of 0 is stepped over) to become the next kick.
The size-0 record ends the session (port 1 = 0, V clear); the routine then clears APUIO2 and returns with RTS. It is the shared low-level routine of SpcLoadBuiltinEngine and SpcBlockTransfer.

blockNote: VBlank synchronization, Mode 7 register upload, and joypad processing with button remapping (163899–164305, Bank 02).
Two entry points share the Mode 7 and joypad pipeline:
- VBlankPartial: skips the NMI wait; its only caller is UpdateFrameFull (system_core), which runs inside the NMI handler
- VBlankWaitAndJoypad: polls RDNMI until VBlank begins, then falls through
=== NMI COOPERATION ===

The hardware joypad value is NOT read here. The NMI handler (step 11) waits for the auto-read to finish and stores JOY1L in joypadRaw; this routine then replaces joypadRaw with the REMAPPED value. It therefore only sees fresh hardware data when the NMI has run since the previous call (NMI enabled while waiting, or called from inside the NMI as VBlankPartial). Called with NMI disabled it would remap an already remapped joypadRaw again, which is not idempotent for swapped or software-only mappings.
=== MODE 7 UPLOAD ===

When scrollModeFlags bit 3 is set, uploads the Mode 7 affine transformation matrix (M7A–M7D) and rotation center (M7X, M7Y) from WRAM shadow registers ($C2–$CD) to PPU write-twice registers ($211B–$2120). Each register requires two consecutive 8-bit writes (low byte, then high byte). Center point high bytes are masked to 5 bits (AND #$1F) for the 13-bit signed coordinate range. Also snapshots BG scroll positions ($BE/$C0 → $CE/$D0) with LDX/STX: X is not saved by this routine, so X is clobbered in Mode 7 scenes (A and P are preserved).
=== JOYPAD INJECT ===

If joypadInject ($09AC) is nonzero, the value becomes joypadCurrent, joypadInject is cleared and the routine returns at once. The injection is one-shot (a script must rewrite it every frame to hold buttons, as sc06_bill does; sg4C_auto_advance writes $FFFF once) and it bypasses everything below: no remapping, no consumption mask, no auto-repeat and no joypadMaskStd, and joypadRaw is left as the hardware value. Writers in extracted/: sg4C_auto_advance, sc06_bill; scene_lifecycle clears it on scene change.
=== BUTTON REMAPPING ===

The D-pad (bits 8–11, $0F00) always passes through directly. Then each physical button is checked against its remap entry: if the button is pressed in joypadRaw and the remap value is nonzero, the remap value (an arbitrary 16-bit logical mask) is TSB'd into joypadRemapped. A button whose remap value is zero never appears. The remap values live in $0DA6–$0DB4 (the diary menu edits them); db-us/transforms.json rewrites some of their defaults. The low nibble of a hardware read is always 0 ($0008/$0004 are not hardware buttons), so a remap target may use those bits as software-only logical buttons.
Remap variable → physical button checked (the names refer to the physical button):
remapStart→Start($1000)  remapSelect→Select($2000)  remapB→B($8000)  remapY→Y($4000)
remapA→A($0080)  remapX→X($0040)  remapL→L($0020)  remapR→R($0010)
SNES joypad bit layout (16-bit auto-read from $4218/$4219):
=== CONSUMPTION MASK + EDGE DETECTION ===
joypadHeld serves as a cooperative consumption mask. Game code marks buttons as consumed via TSB $joypadHeld when processing input events. This routine then:
1. Copies remapped → joypadCurrent and joypadRaw
2. ANDs joypadHeld with the remapped buttons — retains only consumed buttons still physically pressed
3. Applies the auto-repeat rule below (which may drop repeat-eligible bits from joypadHeld)
4. TRBs joypadHeld from joypadCurrent — removes consumed buttons — and then joypadMaskStd
Result: joypadCurrent = newly pressed buttons + auto-repeat triggers. A consumed button does not reappear until it is released and pressed again (or auto-repeat fires).
=== AUTO-REPEAT ===
Buttons in joypadMaskInv (the repeat mask; the dialog handler and the diary menu set it to $0F00, the D-pad) that are consumed and still held are repeat-eligible:
- joypadRepeatCounter increments on each call while at least one is held

- on the 12th call the eligible bits are cleared from joypadHeld BEFORE it is subtracted from joypadCurrent, so the repeat shows up in joypadCurrent in the same call; the counter is reset, so the first repeat comes 12 calls after the press was consumed and the following ones every 12 calls while the game code keeps consuming them
- the counter is also reset whenever no consumed button in the mask is held
joypadMaskStd is TRB'd from joypadCurrent at the end to unconditionally suppress certain buttons (never from the injected value).
=== UTILITY ROUTINES ===
EnableNmiAndJoypad: $81 → NMITIMEN (NMI + joypad auto-read).
EnableNmiOnly: $01 → NMITIMEN. Despite the name this turns the NMI OFF and leaves only joypad auto-read on (see R-I022-1).
ScreenBlackout: $00 → INIDISP (forced blank OFF, brightness 0 — screen appears black but PPU remains active; does NOT set the SNES forced blank bit).
EnterForcedBlank: $80 → INIDISP (forced blank ON — PPU halted, VRAM/OAM/CGRAM accessible for DMA transfers).
WaitFrames: loop VBlankWaitAndJoypad for A frames (A = 0 would wait 256 frames, or 65,536 with a 16-bit A).

partNotes.VBlankPartial: Partial VBlank handler — skips the NMI wait and performs the Mode 7 upload and joypad processing only. Its only caller is UpdateFrameFull (system_core), which the NMI handler runs while a music upload is in progress; the NMI has already stored a fresh joypadRaw by then. Saves P and the 16-bit accumulator (PHA under REP #$20), switches to 8-bit A and branches into the section shared with VBlankWaitAndJoypad.
VBlankWaitAndJoypad: Full VBlank synchronization with Mode 7 register upload and joypad input processing.

Polls RDNMI ($4210) until bit 7 is set (VBlank started), then falls through to the Mode 7 upload and the complete joypad pipeline: inject check, button remapping, consumption mask update, auto-repeat, and edge detection.

RDNMI is read before the loop (clears a stale flag), in the loop, and once more after it; reading the register clears the flag, so the extra read after the loop changes nothing. The caller normally has NMI enabled while it waits, so the NMI handler runs inside the poll loop and refreshes joypadRaw before the remap below. Saves and restores A and P only (see the block note for the X clobber in Mode 7).
See the vblank_joypad block note for detailed descriptions of each pipeline stage.
EnableNmiOnly: Write $01 to NMITIMEN ($4200): joypad auto-read ON, NMI OFF.

Bit 7 clear disables the NMI; bit 0 keeps the joypad auto-read enabled. The name is misleading (R-I022-1): the routine is called after the main loop's VBlank sync so that the frame's logic runs without NMI interruption, and by the SPC transfer routines around the port handshakes. EnableNmiAndJoypad turns the NMI back on.
WaitFrames: Wait for A frames by calling VBlankWaitAndJoypad in a loop.

Entry: A = number of frames to wait (A = 0 would wait 256 frames with an 8-bit A, 65,536 with a 16-bit A). VBlankWaitAndJoypad preserves A, so the DEC counts the frames. Joypad state is updated every frame during the wait only if the NMI runs (see the block note).
